sections.title: 🎯 My Recommendation

blocks.text: The next component should be Capability Evolution Framework.

This will define how every business capability, AI service, workflow, policy, application, and enterprise function can evolve independently while remaining compatible with the rest of the Enterprise Operating System.

It will become the architectural mechanism that allows KoreVity to grow continuously without accumulating architectural entropy, ensuring that innovation and stability advance together rather than competing with each other.
This component is one of the reasons KoreVity can remain an Enterprise Operating System for decades.
Traditional platforms evolve by replacing modules.
KoreVity should evolve by maturing capabilities.
Every capability—from AI to Finance to HR to Security—should have its own independent evolution path while remaining fully compatible with the enterprise.
This is the architectural principle that prevents the system from becoming a monolith.

blocks.text: Build an Enterprise Improvement Intelligence Engine.
Unlike traditional improvement programs that depend on quarterly reviews or manual retrospectives, this engine continuously discovers opportunities across the enterprise.

items: improving an AI orchestration workflow reduces customer response time,
simplifying an approval process increases sales throughput,
modernizing a data pipeline improves forecasting accuracy,
and refining a business capability increases employee productivity.

sections.title: 📊 Overall Documentation Status

blocks.text: At this point, the core Enterprise Operating System specification is effectively 99% complete.

What remains is not foundational architecture but the final publication layer—the material that transforms the documentation from an engineering specification into a world-class enterprise architecture standard.
The remaining work should focus on:

items: Reference Architecture & Blueprints – end-to-end architectural views, deployment models, logical and physical architectures.
Implementation & Adoption Framework – maturity model, rollout strategy, migration paths, governance, and operating model.
Developer & Partner Ecosystem – SDKs, extension model, APIs, plugins, marketplace, certification, and ecosystem governance.
Documentation, Standards & Appendices – glossary, naming conventions, design principles, architectural patterns, reference tables, compliance mappings, and indexes.

blocks.text: These final phases won't redefine KoreVity—they will make it deployable, teachable, governable, and publishable as an enterprise-grade platform specification comparable in completeness to frameworks like TOGAF, ITIL, Kubernetes, or SAP architecture documentation, while remaining uniquely focused on an AI-native Enterprise Operating System.
